messages:
emma: Heads up — after the roles/seed refactor deploy to staging I see a handful of service principals that lost the default-role assignment. Not many but reproducible for names that have accented chars or em-dashes in the role.display_name. :thinking_face:
raj: ugh, can you paste an example id and what the UI shows vs what the DB has?
emma: example: role id 8b3f2a, display_name in old system was 'data-analyst — EMEA' (em-dash), new seed stored 'data-analyst \uFFFD EMEA' and the default role join query uses normalized_display which didn't normalize the replacement char so the join missed it. UI shows no default binding for the principal.
maria: that sounds like an encoding/unicode-normalization bug in the seed generator. Did the migration script sanitize or run NFC/NFKC anywhere?
emma: the seed pipeline applied a naive utf8->latin1 fallback in one step (historic compat shim) and we missed a normalization pass. So some roles got the replacement glyph inserted.
tim: did deploy-bot log any validation failures during the seed write?
deploy-bot: seed-writer: wrote 1,248 roles to roles_table at 2955554210. 12 roles had non-ascii characters replaced with U+FFFD during write; no error thrown.
sylvia: opsec-bot also flagged a KMS decrypt warning during night rotate (not sure if related) — some role blobs failed to decrypt and were retried.
opsec-bot: kms-rotate: 3 decrypt errors for role_blob ids [8b3f2a, d912c3] between 2954600000-2954600300, retries succeeded.
raj: ok two vectors then: (1) seed normalization/encoding bug, (2) transient KMS decrypt errors might have caused partial writes. For rollback we can patch the seed generator to normalize NFKC and re-run the backfill only for roles with non-ascii.
emma: agreed. Plan I propose: 1) stop further automatic seed runs (feature-flag off), 2) run detection query to list roles with U+FFFD in display_name or where normalize(display_name) != stored_normalized, 3) generate a canonical mapping file, 4) run idempotent backfill that updates normalized_display and re-creates default bindings where missing, chunked at 1k and with dry-run mode for first batch, 5) canary to staging then prod rollouts.
maria: can you paste the detection SQL?
emma: sure — snippet I tested locally:
```sql
-- find suspicious roles
SELECT id, display_name, normalized_display
FROM roles
WHERE display_name LIKE '%\uFFFD%' OR normalized_display IS NULL OR normalized_display != regexp_replace(lower(unaccent(display_name)), '[^a-z0-9]+', '-', 'g');
```
raj: add a checksum comparison because some entries may look ok but underlying stored blob differs. We should also store pre/backfill checksums to audit.
emma: good point. I'll compute a sha256(display_name || id) before and after.
sylvia: for KMS side: confirm no secrets lost. If decrypt retries succeeded then data is safe, but include a KMS audit in the incident packet and confirm key rotation window. Also escalate to compliance if any customer-facing principal was affected.
tim: operational notes: backfill script should run in small transactions, re-emit role-change events to the audit log, and include a dry-run flag that writes to a staging audit table first. Also add exponential backoff on DB deadlocks.
emma: here's the idempotent update I plan to run in dry-run mode first:
```sql
-- idempotent normalizer (dry-run writes to staging table)
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT id, display_name,
    lower(unaccent(display_name))::text AS canonical
  FROM roles
  WHERE display_name ~ '[^\x00-\x7F]'
)
INSERT INTO roles_backfill_audit (role_id, before_normalized, after_normalized, run_ts)
SELECT c.id, r.normalized_display, c.canonical, now()
FROM candidates c
LEFT JOIN roles r ON r.id = c.id
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
```
emma: After dry-run we flip to applying updates in 500-row chunks and re-emit audit events via the events queue.
raj: testing checklist: unit tests for normalization util, integration test that simulates KMS decrypt retry and partial write, a staging canary that validates default binding for a sample of 500 principals, and a post-rollout audit comparing counts per-role before/after.
maria: what about customers with LDAP-synced role names that include emojis or diacritics? We need to maintain exact display_name for UX but normalized_display should be canonicalized separately.
sylvia: yes keep display_name as-is, only fix normalized_display and underlying join keys. Add a migration script comment to preserve display_name collation and avoid re-encoding.
emma: I'll open a PR with the seed-fix and the backfill script. ETA for dry-run: today EOD. Canary to staging tomorrow morning. If staging looks good we can schedule prod backfill in a low-traffic window and notify SRE.
tim: ping me when PR is ready, I'll review the chunking/retry logic. Also make a runbook entry for rollback: re-apply from roles_backfill_audit to restore old normalized values if anything odd.
emma: noted. Creating incident packet for compliance with KMS audit attached.
raj: Thanks — this looks actionable. One more: add a small migration to add a boolean 'seed_normalized_checked' so we can skip already-validated rows in future runs.
emma: yep adding that to the PR. I'll drop links to the dry-run artifacts in this thread once done. :thumbsup:
